title: Win+H remapping forces the user to hold the new shortcut

status.label: Needs a current Win+H comparison
status.detail: The report is from v0.83.0 and does not identify the Windows build or whether a direct Win+H tap has the same release behavior.

next_action.label: Compare native and remapped Win+H on current stable
next_action.reason: A current comparison will show whether the release behavior comes from Keyboard Manager or the Windows voice-typing hotkey on this system.

actions.label: Compare native and remapped Win+H on current stable

comment.body: Thanks for the exact steps; the attached screenshot confirms the remap is Win+Z to Win+H. The report is from v0.83.0, and the issue does not say which Windows build is handling the Win+H voice-typing shortcut. Could you confirm whether this still occurs on v0.102.3001 and provide your Windows version/build? On that setup, please compare a tap of native Win+H with a tap and a hold of the remapped Win+Z, and report whether voice typing remains open and accepts input in each case.

judgment.rationale: The attached screenshot confirms the remapping is Win+Z to Win+H, and the report says releasing Win+Z immediately closes Speech Recognition instead of leaving it ready for dictation. The report is from v0.83.0, has no comments, and gives no Windows build. A native Win+H comparison is needed to separate a Keyboard Manager key-release issue from Windows voice-typing behavior on the reporter's system.
evidence: The issue body lists PowerToys v0.83.0 and says the replacement shortcut is intended to open Speech Recognition.
The attached screenshot shows Win+Z mapped to Win+H for all apps.
The reporter says Speech Recognition closes as soon as the replacement shortcut is released.
The report has no Windows version/build or discussion, and no matching issue or PR was found in the focused search.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a current-build comparison of native Win+H and the remapped Win+Z, including the Windows version/build and tap-versus-hold results.

fix_assessment.rationale: If native Win+H stays active but Win+Z-to-Win+H closes on release on the current build, Keyboard Manager may be releasing the target shortcut in a way that changes the system hotkey's expected behavior. The Windows build and native baseline are not yet known.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Win+H behavior when a replacement shortcut is released
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remapping path may send a target key-up that causes Windows voice typing to close immediately, but the issue does not establish whether native Win+H has the same behavior on the reported Windows version.
plan: Compare native Win+H and the reported Win+Z-to-Win+H remap on the current Windows and PowerToys builds.
If only the remapped shortcut closes on release, trace the key-down/key-up handling for the generated Win+H chord.
Adjust the narrow remapping behavior so the target system hotkey remains active after the replacement shortcut is tapped, without changing ordinary held-key semantics.
Add a regression test for Win+Z-to-Win+H tap and hold behavior.
verification: On a supported Windows build, a tap of the remapped Win+Z opens voice typing and leaves it ready to accept dictation, matching the expected native behavior.
Holding and releasing the remapped shortcut does not leave Win or H stuck and does not alter unrelated shortcut remaps.

confidence.rationale: The screenshot and report identify the exact target chord and release symptom, but there is no current-version repro or native Win+H baseline to confirm the owning behavior.

issue_context.summary: A Win+Z-to-Win+H mapping reportedly opens Speech Recognition only while Win+Z is held and closes it immediately on release.
known_information: The screenshot shows Win+Z mapped to Win+H for all apps.
The reporter expects voice typing to remain open after a tap and says it closes on release.
A screenshot and a short recording are attached; there are no issue comments.
The Windows version/build and current-version result are not present.
inferences: If direct Win+H remains active while the remapped chord closes, target key-release handling in Keyboard Manager is a plausible cause.
If direct Win+H also closes on release, the behavior may instead be specific to the Windows voice-typing implementation or configuration.
issue_context.analysis: The screenshot confirms the exact mapping, but the missing Windows build and native-hotkey baseline prevent attribution. The next discriminating evidence is a tap/hold comparison of native Win+H and remapped Win+Z on current stable; another generic diagnostics request is not justified.
initial_investigation: Refreshed the full issue body and confirmed it has no comments or assignee.
Inspected the attached screenshot, confirming Win+Z is mapped to Win+H for all apps.
Searched for other PowerToys reports and PRs about remapped Win+H voice typing; no matching item was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the behavior still occurs on v0.102.3001, the Windows version/build, and the tap-versus-hold result for native Win+H versus remapped Win+Z
information_gaps.why_needed: The Windows hotkey may have build-specific behavior; a native comparison is required to isolate whether the remapping path changes the release semantics.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, compare a tap of native Win+H with a tap and hold of the remapped Win+Z, then report whether voice typing remains open and accepts input for each.
